Banished

For a few hours this is an interesting city building/city survival experience, but after that flaws with the population and mechanics start to come through that ruin the long-term experience. It also doesn't cater to large-scale city design, so I'm not sure that it really has the replayability found in normal city building games.

 

Legend of Grimrock

The sequel for this game is out, and it's better in every way - but this is still a decent buy if you want to test the genre and see if you enjoy it. There aren't too many games that combine grid-based movement with real time combat, and it has a unique feel.

This game is all in a dark dungeon though - so if you're looking for beautiful outside environments you'll have to play the sequel.

 

Legend of Grimrock 2

An excellent sequel to Legend of Grimrock. The first game was all inside a dark dungeon, and this one expands to a colorful outside world - while still keeping the semi-turn based grid combat.

This is the best game I've played in the party-dungeon-crawler genre, and I'd heartily recommend giving it a shot if you like these. It has some light puzzles to keep everything interesting as well.

 

Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition

A lot of people love the Dark Souls series, it's one of those games you'll either love or hate. Personally I didn't enjoy it - the basic enemies respawn when you die or use a save point, and this makes attempting to kill a boss multiple times kind of a hassle.

Imagine having to reclear trash every time you wanted to kill a boss in World of Warcraft, that would be insanely tedious. Additionally if you want to play the game you'll need to mod it, since the resolution is locked to something atrociously low. You'll also want a game controller, the keyboard is known to be subpar for this game.

So pick this one up if you have a lot of patience, and get satisfaction from trying hard challenges and eventually beating them. Otherwise you may want to give it a pass.

 

Bioshock Triple Pack

BioShock 1 is an FPS with a great atmosphere and unique environment, the only thing I really had an issue with were the big daddies - which were frustrating to fight.

Infinite had combat that was very similar to a normal FPS, and again had an interesting world. Additionally you get a brilliant AI companion, although mid-game it does start feeling a bit fetch-questish.

 

Darksiders

The world in this hack-n-slash is pretty cool, and the weapons are satisfying. It is quite linear, but they designed it well enough that it doesn't feel like a corridor - and I actually got a good Legend Of Zelda vibe from it. If you like those type of games this series might be worth a look.

 

Red Faction Collection

I've only played Red Faction 1 and Armageddon, but the whole series is really known for how destructible the environments are in the games. The first one is quite old and pretty innovative in that respect, you can tunnel through most of the rock in the game using your weapons.

Armageddon prevents terrain destruction but even massive buildings can be knocked down, and it's pretty cool to see - although the camera is a tight-third person view like console games. That makes it a bit more annoying than it should be.

The enemies in this game are pretty easy, and in many places you can just run past them until you hit one of the numerous cutscenes (which despawns everything chasing you). Weapons are also limited, 4 slots. It's very obviously a console experience, and has a lot of strange design decisions that seem more like they were focused on the technical aspects of the game instead of making sure it was fun.

 

Shadow Warrior

A first person hack-n-slash with a humorous protagonist. The story is a ludicrous Japanese tale of ninjas and demons, but the main draw is your character's sardonic remarks about the situation. The swordplay is pretty solid as well.

 

Walking Dead

Obviously this series is known for having a good story - it's basically a choose your own adventure game with point-and-click elements. The downside is that a lot of your choices have no real relevance to the story - often they just choose which of your companions is present during the journey, not what actually happens.

This lack of actual choice was a bit disappointing, but the story is still interesting - so if linearity doesn't bother you it may still be worth a look.

 

Mark of the Ninja

This wasn't a bad game, but I didn't enjoy the feel of it - that ninja feeling just didn't come through for me.

 

Outlast

Horror that's more frustrating than scary - I spent most of the time cheesing the enemies by running in circles rather than wasting an absurd amount of time hiding. There are only one or two jump scares, and the game didn't really get good until the very last level in my opinion.

If all the levels had the theme and sense of urgency found in the last level it would have been a far better and more interesting experience.

 

Killing Floor

The sequel to this game is currently in early access (probably for the next 6 months), but for a couple bucks this is a great co-op experience. You fight off hordes of zombies with different special abilities, working to use your classes together. One person might be the sharpshooter, another might take out big enemies with shotguns, and a third person might light all the small ones on fire with a flamethrower.

It's important to level up, because you get perks as you get to higher levels - for example the firebug's smg starts lighting things on fire, and he gets complete immunity to flaming enemies. The only downside is that this leveling can take a long time for some classes - and that's one of the things they're improving in the sequel.

 

Trine2

I actually prefer this original game to the sequel - it felt a lot more like an adventure through a sandbox, rather than the forced linear nature of some of the sequel puzzles. I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game though - most of it is about platforming while killing enemies.

 

Trine

I actually prefer this original game to the sequel - it felt a lot more like an adventure through a sandbox, rather than the forced linear nature of some of the sequel puzzles. I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game though - most of it is about platforming while killing enemies.

 

Limbo

This linear little platformer is a dark journey full of death, and a pretty fun time if you like casual puzzle platforming. It has great atmosphere, and is definitely worth the couple dollar pricetag from this sale.

 

The Fall

This game had terrible controls but was a great experience. It really should have been a point-and-click, but once you get past that the sci-fi atmosphere is really great, and the story is enjoyable.

The basic premise is that you're a sentient space suit whose owner has passed out, and you're trying to rescue him. One of my top picks last year.

 

Braid

I think this was the first game that used time reversal as a crucial mechanic, and the puzzle element of it is pretty good. Since you can reverse time it never gets frustrating when an enemy kills you, just step back a few seconds and try again. The story is a bit weird though and really didn't grab my attention. Even by the end of the game you may not fully understand it.

 

Orcs Must Die 2

This is a decent co-op experience - which the original game didn't have - but it lacks the great sense of humor that game had. And that was what really made the previous one shine in my opinion, without that it's just a solid first-person tower defense.

 

Shadow of Mordor

The gameplay in this was solid, with the overall collectibles and roaming feeling very much like Assassin's Creed. The combat was pretty easy - somewhat satisfying but would have been better if there was actually a chance of you dieing in a swarm of enemies. Currently you can just dash around and hop over dudes and be nearly invincible unless you mess up. Fun, but not difficult.

My video review is also based on the main game - there have been DLC that may have completed the story, but the main game itself kind of leaves you hanging.

 

The Swapper

Sure, this is a puzzle game, but the thing that really appealed to me was the atmosphere. They do a great job of making you feel truly alone in an abandoned space, and just for that alone it's worth trying.

 

Just Cause 2

Single-player mayhem with an over-the-top story, this is an all-around great experience. There is a multiplayer mod, but they haven't really fixed the bugs enough for it to be a proper multiplayer experience - I'd still classify this as a mainly single-player game.

It's a really good one though, and if you haven't played it I'd definitely recommend picking it up. Don't worry, it still looks pretty nice even though it came out 5 years ago.

 

Auditorium

This one was a pretty great music puzzle game where you have to arrange circles of sound/color properly to finish the level. It's only $0.69 and I'd highly recommend picking it up if you like music-based games.
